title: Human Capital section added; Item 1A grouped into categories; Solorigate and Exchange attacks named; ZeniMax and Nuance added
sub: Filed Jul 2021 | Headcount: 163,000 → 181,000 | Revenue: $143.0B → $168.1B | Commercial cloud revenue: $51.7B → $69.1B
era_summary: FY2021 adds a Human Capital Resources section, groups risk factors under seven category headings, and names the Solorigate/Nobelium and Exchange Server attacks. ZeniMax (completed March 2021, $8.1 billion) and Nuance (agreement April 2021, $19.7 billion) appear in Business, Risk Factors and MD&A. MD&A cites the server useful-life change as a driver of margins and operating income, and the capital-expenditure outlook sentence is unchanged.

findings.title: Cloud position claim: "one of the two largest providers … we believe" → "the most comprehensive and trusted cloud"
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "As one of the two largest providers of cloud computing at scale, we believe we work from a position of strength."
FY2021: "The Microsoft Cloud is the most comprehensive and trusted cloud, providing the best integration across the technology stack while offering openness, improving time to value, reducing costs, and increasing agility."

findings.title: Opening line: "continue to transform our business to lead in" → "are living in" the new era
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "We continue to transform our business to lead in the new era of the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge."
FY2021: "We are living in the new era of the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge, which is being sharpened by rapid advances in distributed computing, ambient intelligence, and multidevice experiences."

findings.title: Supply chain: "only one qualified supplier" for "the majority" → "very few qualified suppliers" for "some"
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "We generally have the ability to use other manufacturers if a current vendor becomes unavailable or unable to meet our requirements. The majority of our hardware products contain components for which there is only one qualified supplier."
FY2021: "For the majority of our products, we have the ability to use other manufacturers if a current vendor becomes unavailable or unable to meet our requirements. However, some of our products contain certain components for which there are very few qualified suppliers. For these components, we have limited near-term flexibility to use other manufacturers if a current vendor becomes unavailable or is unable to meet our requirements."

The same supply-chain paragraph is added to MD&A Economic Conditions in FY2021.

findings.title: Nuance acquisition agreement and ZeniMax acquisition added
findings.body_html:
FY2021: "In April 2021, we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications, Inc., a cloud and AI software provider with healthcare and enterprise AI experience. The acquisition will build on our industry-specific cloud offerings."
FY2021: "We have a strong position with our large and growing highly engaged community of gamers, including the March 2021 acquisition of ZeniMax Media Inc., the parent company of Bethesda Softworks LLC, one of the largest, privately held game developers and publishers in the world."

findings.title: Hybrid consistency list reordered: security moves first; "data" and "compute" dropped; "compliance" added
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "Our hybrid infrastructure consistency spans identity, data, compute, management, and security, helping to support the real-world needs and evolving regulatory requirements of commercial customers and enterprises."
FY2021: "Our hybrid infrastructure consistency spans security, compliance, identity, and management, helping to support the real-world needs and evolving regulatory requirements of commercial customers and enterprises."

findings.title: "manufacture" removed from "design, manufacture, and sell devices" (twice)
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "We also design, manufacture, and sell devices, including PCs, tablets, gaming and entertainment consoles, other intelligent devices, and related accessories."
FY2021: "We also design and sell devices, including PCs, tablets, gaming and entertainment consoles, other intelligent devices, and related accessories."

The same edit is made in the Devices subsection and in the Risk Factors quality/supply factor.

findings.title: Xbox Game Pass member count removed; gaming approach "are broadening" → "have broadened"
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "Xbox Game Pass, with over 10 million members from 41 countries, is a community with access to a curated library of over 100 first- and third-party console and PC titles."
FY2021: "Xbox Game Pass is a community with access to a curated library of over 100 first- and third-party console and PC titles."
FY2020: "We are broadening our approach to how we think about gaming end-to-end, from the way games are created and distributed to how they are played and viewed across PC, console, and mobile."
FY2021: "We have broadened our approach to how we think about gaming end-to-end, from the way games are created and distributed to how they are played, including cloud gaming so players can stream across PC, console, and mobile."

FY2021: "As part of our effort to promote a One Microsoft and inclusive culture, we expanded stock eligibility to all Microsoft employees as part of our annual rewards process."

findings.title: Item 1A grouped under seven category sub-headings for the first time
findings.body_html: FY2020 is a flat list. FY2021 headings: STRATEGIC AND COMPETITIVE RISKS; RISKS RELATING TO THE EVOLUTION OF OUR BUSINESS; CYBERSECURITY, DATA PRIVACY, AND PLATFORM ABUSE RISKS; OPERATIONAL RISKS; LEGAL, REGULATORY, AND LITIGATION RISKS; INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RISKS; GENERAL RISKS. The three IP factors, "Claims and lawsuits", "Government customers" and the global-business factor are relocated; the first seven factors keep their positions.

findings.title: Solorigate/Nobelium supply-chain attack and nation-state actors added
findings.body_html:
FY2021: "Nation state and state sponsored actors can deploy significant resources to plan and carry out exploits."
FY2021: "The cyberattacks uncovered in late 2020 known as “Solorigate” or “Nobelium” are an example of a supply chain attack where malware was introduced to a software provider’s customers, including us, through software updates."
FY2021: "We may be targets of further attacks similar to Solorigate/Nobelium as both a supplier and consumer of IT."

findings.title: Exchange Server on-premises zero-day exploitation named; "Adversaries will continue to attack"
findings.body_html:
FY2021: "In addition, adversaries can attack our customers’ on-premises or cloud environments, sometimes exploiting previously unknown (“zero day”) vulnerabilities, such as occurred in early calendar year 2021 with several of our Exchange Server on-premises products."
FY2021: "Adversaries will continue to attack customers using our cloud services as customers embrace digital transformation."

findings.title: AI and content-moderation regulation: "could also emerge" → "is emerging"
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "Legislative or regulatory action could also emerge in the area of AI and content moderation, increasing costs or restricting opportunity."
FY2021: "Legislative and regulatory action is emerging in the areas of AI and content moderation, which could increase costs or restrict opportunity."

findings.title: Trade paragraph rewritten: export and import controls added; Sudan dropped from sanctions list
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "Operations outside the U.S. may be affected by changes in trade protection laws, policies, sanctions, and other regulatory requirements affecting trade and investment."
FY2021: "Increasing trade laws, policies, sanctions, and other regulatory requirements also affect our operations in and outside the U.S."
FY2021: "U.S. export controls restrict Microsoft from offering many of its products and services to, or making investments in, certain entities in specified countries. U.S. import controls restrict us from integrating certain information and communication technologies into our supply chain"
FY2021: "Economic sanctions in the U.S., the EU, and other countries prohibit most business with restricted entities or countries such as Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Syria."

FY2020 listed "Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, and Syria". The factor caption changes "liability" → "consequences" and "trade protection" → "trade".

findings.title: Global business factor: "geopolitical" risks, "protectionist" trends and human-rights concerns added
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "The global nature of our business creates operational and economic risks."
FY2021: "The global nature of our business creates operational, economic, and geopolitical risks."
FY2020: "Emerging nationalist trends in specific countries may significantly alter the trade environment."
FY2021: "Emerging nationalist and protectionist trends and concerns about human rights and political expression in specific countries may significantly alter the trade and commercial environments."

findings.title: Segment revenue drivers: IC "server products and cloud services" → "Azure"; MPC "Windows and Surface" → "Gaming"
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "Intelligent Cloud revenue increased, driven by server products and cloud services."
FY2021: "Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure."
FY2020: "More Personal Computing revenue increased, driven by Windows and Surface."
FY2021: "More Personal Computing revenue increased driven by Gaming."

findings.title: Server useful-life change: "it is estimated … will increase" → "the effect … was an increase" with net income and EPS
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "…it is estimated this change will increase our fiscal year 2021 operating income by $2.7 billion."
FY2021: "…the effect of this change in estimate for fiscal year 2021 was an increase in operating income of $2.7 billion and net income of $2.3 billion, or $0.30 per both basic and diluted share."

FY2021 cites the useful-life change as a driver of cost of revenue, gross margin, gross margin percentage, commercial cloud gross margin percentage, operating income, and PBP and IC gross margin.

findings.title: Commercial cloud gross margin: 67% → 71%; "sales mix shift to Azure" added as an offset
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "Commercial cloud gross margin percentage increased 4 points to 67%, primarily driven by improvement in Azure."
FY2021: "Commercial cloud gross margin percentage increased 4 points to 71% driven by gross margin percentage improvement in Azure and the change in estimated useful lives of our server and network equipment, offset in part by sales mix shift to Azure."
FY2021: "Excluding this impact, gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by gross margin percentage reduction in More Personal Computing."

findings.title: MPC gross margin percentage: "increased" → "decreased" on Gaming hardware mix
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "Gross margin percentage increased, due to sales mix shift to higher margin businesses and gross margin percentage improvement in Gaming."
FY2021: "Gross margin percentage decreased driven by sales mix shift to Gaming hardware."
FY2021: "Xbox hardware revenue increased 92% driven by higher price of consoles sold due to the Xbox Series X|S launches."

findings.body_html: FY2021: "The acquisition has been approved by Nuance’s shareholders, and we expect it to close by the end of calendar year 2021, subject to the satisfaction of certain regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions."

findings.title: China SAMR: "has presented its preliminary views … discussions are expected to continue" → "In 2019, the SAMR presented"
findings.body_html:
FY2020: "The SAMR has presented its preliminary views as to certain possible violations of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, and discussions are expected to continue."

findings.title: Cell phone litigation: 40 → 46 lawsuits; hearing "expected to occur" → "scheduled for January and February of 2022"
findings.body_html:

FY2020: "A hearing is expected to occur in the second quarter of fiscal year 2021"
